html:
A long Ottoman siege of Thessalonica, the second city of the Byzantine world, from 1422 until the Ottomans stormed it in 1430.

Murad II blockaded the city in 1422 at the same time as he besieged Constantinople. Its Byzantine governor, Andronikos Palaiologos, could not hold it, and in 1423 he handed it to Venice, hoping the republic could defend it.

Venice held on for seven years at great cost, but it could not break the blockade or buy peace. The townspeople grew hungry, and some favoured surrender. On 29 March 1430 Murad's army took the city by storm and sacked it. Thousands were enslaved. An eyewitness, John Anagnostes, wrote an account of the fall.

Thessalonica stayed Ottoman until 1912. Its fall was a rehearsal for the fall of Constantinople 23 years later.
sum: A long Ottoman siege of Thessalonica, the second city of the Byzantine world, from 1422 until the Ottomans stormed it in 1430.
